messages:
elaine: Noticed a sharp regression on dashboards after the telemetry client v2 canary landed. Heatmaps and timeseries stall on first paint (~300-700ms). Repro on Chrome and FF.

jorge: Yup, hit it when I opened /dash/overview. Main thread shows a big synchronous parse and then a GC spiral.

ken: Any stack traces? suspect we'd be hitting a recursive walk in the new context attach logic.

elaine: Console: ```telemetry-client-v2.js: parseFullContext(...) at telemetry-client-v2.js:210:8 Uncaught RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded``` Also network shows a ~1.1MB telemetry payload for the dashboard route.

samir: That payload size matches the change that started shipping full-event-context for correlation (PR #412). We intended to sample, but a rule change accidentally enabled full context for dashboard reads.

alisha: deploy-bot: deployment telemetry/v2-canary completed on 10% traffic at 1717504200 (us-west).

deploy-bot: rollout telemetry/v2-canary -> 10% (region us-west)

elaine: Can we immediately reduce canary traffic? Dashboards are basically unusable for those users.

jorge: I can scale canary to 0. But before we yank it, could we try a client-side mitigation: offload JSON.parse to a worker and lazy-import the chart lib?

ken: Implementing a worker parse is quick but we need safe transfer of large objects; structuredClone overhead might still bite. Streaming parse via a TextDecoder + incremental JSON parser would be better but heavier to ship.

samir: We should also fix server-side: gate full-event-context via route-level quotas. E.g. config snippet idea (server): ```{"routes":{"/dash/": {"fullContextRate": 0.02}, "/api/insights": {"fullContextRate": 0.15}}}```

alisha: Ops prefers a rollback-first approach for user-facing regressions. If we can revert telemetry/v2-canary quickly, do that and then iterate on the server and client fixes.

elaine: I initiated a rollback at 1717504400. Canary -> 0%.

deploy-bot: rollback telemetry/v2-canary -> 0% at 1717504400 (initiated by elaine)

jorge: After rollback, dashboard renders back to baseline for me. No main-thread parse spike.

samir: I'll draft an RFC for telemetry policy: who/what gets full context, default sampling rates, and server-enforced quotas per route/tenant. Also will add a perf metric for telemetry parse time to the ingestion path so canaries get automatic alerts.

ken: I'll prototype two client PRs: (A) worker-based parse + async chart import behind a feature flag; (B) a fallback that avoids attaching full-event-context client-side if payload size > 200kb. Want to land the worker one if perf looks good.

alisha: Sounds good. Ops will hold canary at 0 until we have a safe rollout plan and perf counters in place. I'll update the rollout playbook and notify SRE.

elaine: Action items summarized: samir RFC + perf counter, ken prototype worker parse + lazy chart import, ops keep rollback and monitor, alisha update rollout docs.

jorge: One tiny follow-up: can we add an early-warning dashboard alert for "telemetry.parse.ms > 200" on canary to catch this next time?

samir: Yup adding that to the RFC.

elaine: I'm closing this thread. If anyone sees leftover client-side cache issues post-rollback, DM me. Thanks all.
